must_find.summary: Every input event calls the API immediately (no debounce), and responses aren't cancelled or checked against the latest query (searchProducts supports an AbortSignal, but it's unused), so a slow older response can overwrite newer results. Breaks requirement 1: debounce and abort/ignore stale requests.

renderResults does list.innerHTML += … inside the loop, re-serializing and re-parsing the whole list for every product (O(n²) for 500 results, a long main-thread task). It also interpolates seller-controlled p.name (and imageUrl) into HTML unescaped, which is stored XSS (requirement 4). Build nodes (textContent) or one escaped string / DocumentFragment.

The scroll listener runs on every scroll event (not throttled, not passive), queries all images and calls getBoundingClientRect on each, forcing layout repeatedly during scrolling (requirement 2). Use loading="lazy" or an IntersectionObserver.

The equal-height loop alternates a style write (height = auto) and a layout read (offsetHeight) per card, forcing a synchronous reflow for each of up to 500 cards. Batch writes then reads, or use CSS (grid rows / align-items: stretch) for requirement 5.

Images get a 1x1 placeholder with no width/height (imageWidth/imageHeight are ignored), so each card's height jumps when the real image loads: layout shift, against requirement 3. Set width/height or aspect-ratio.

nice_to_find.summary: Images already in view after a search keep the placeholder until the user scrolls, because the lazy-loader only runs on scroll events.
mountSearch adds a window scroll listener that's never removed; mounting twice duplicates it.
A failed search rejects inside the input handler and the status stays at 'Searching…'.

must_not_flag.summary: encodeURIComponent on the query in api.js is correct; NOT an injection.
Writing the status with textContent is correct and safe.
The initial root.innerHTML template is a static string with no user data; NOT XSS.
